findings.title: Deleting the cache never invalidates connectedCalendars, so the UI keeps showing a stale cache status
findings.body: `deleteCacheMutation` only shows a toast and calls the optional `onSuccess`. The disconnect mutation next to it invalidates `viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars` in `onSettled` (lines 61-64); this one invalidates nothing. In the event type Advanced tab (`packages/features/eventtypes/components/tabs/advanced/EventAdvancedTab.tsx:372-377`), `SelectedCalendarsSettingsWebWrapper` gets no `onChanged`, so nothing refetches. The query also uses `refetchOnWindowFocus: false`. The result: after a successful delete, the dropdown still shows "Last updated: …" and the delete option, which tells the user the cache still exists. Fix: invalidate `utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars` in this mutation's `onSettled`, as the disconnect mutation does.

findings.title: Empty-data updateMany on every cache refresh, and the UI never reads its result
findings.body: `updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {})` runs a write on every `fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache` (webhooks and cron), relying on Prisma to bump `SelectedCalendar.updatedAt` from an empty `data`. I'm not sure Prisma issues an UPDATE at all when `data` is empty. Either way, the cache status the UI shows comes from `CalendarCache.updatedAt` (`calendar-cache.repository.ts:173-187`), and the `upsertCachedAvailability` upsert already sets that. Nothing in this PR reads the newly selected `SelectedCalendar.updatedAt`. Consider dropping this call, or setting `updatedAt: new Date()` explicitly if it is really needed.

findings.title: Cache timestamp is always formatted as en-US
findings.body: `new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", …)` ignores the user's locale and profile time zone, while the label around it is translated. Consider using the locale from `useLocale()` (`i18n.language`) instead.

findings.title: Cache status counts expired rows
findings.body: `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` takes `_max(updatedAt)` over every CalendarCache row of the credential, including rows past `expiresAt`. So the UI can report a cache that is no longer used. Also, the migration backfills `updatedAt` with NOW() for legacy rows, so right after deploy every existing cache shows as "updated" at migration time. Consider filtering on `expiresAt > now()`.

findings.title: Delete-cache action now appears where connection modification is disabled
findings.body: Before, no action was rendered when `disableConnectionModification` was true (the event type Advanced tab). Now the dropdown renders there whenever a Google cache exists, and it offers the destructive "Delete cached data" action. Is exposing cache deletion on the event type page intended?

findings.title: Script only works on macOS and from one directory
findings.body: `sed -i ''` is BSD syntax: GNU sed treats `''` as a file name and fails. `ENV_FILE="../.env"` is resolved against the current directory, not the script's location, so running the script from the repository root writes to the directory above the repository. Consider resolving the path from `$(dirname "$0")` and using a portable in-place edit.

contracts.action: Delete cached data for a credential
contracts.equivalent_path: Disconnect credential mutation in the same dropdown
contracts.before_after: The handler checks that the credential belongs to the user (id + userId), then runs deleteMany on CalendarCache by credentialId. The check and the delete happen in the same request, and the delete removes only that credential's cache rows. The client does not invalidate connectedCalendars, while the disconnect mutation does.
contracts.visible_effect: Shows a toast; the cache status stays stale unless the parent passes onChanged (EventAdvancedTab does not).
contracts.failure_mode: If the credential is not found, the handler throws a generic Error; the client shows the error toast. If the delete fails, the error toast appears and no state is lost, since the cache simply refills.

contracts.before_after: Builds a repository with a null calendar; the groupBy needs no calendar, so this is safe.
contracts.visible_effect: The dropdown shows the last-updated timestamp for Google credentials.
contracts.failure_mode: If the groupBy fails, the whole connectedCalendars query fails.

summary: The main problem: the new delete-cache mutation never invalidates the connectedCalendars query. On the event type Advanced tab, where no onChanged is passed, the cache status stays stale after a delete. The other findings are worth considering but none blocks the merge: an empty-data updateMany runs on every cache refresh and nothing reads its result; the timestamp is always formatted as en-US; the cache status counts expired rows, and migrated legacy rows show the migration time; the delete action is now exposed on the event type page; and the helper script only works on macOS and assumes a fixed working directory.
